Publish values by name

Source: R/values.R
weft_put.Rd

weft_put() publishes R values under names, so that prose can refer to them by name: a code span holding the name, with a formatter class, `depth`{.num}. The values travel in a weft-values block, which the resolver filter reads (rules 2.13, 3.8). In an R document the hooks publish a name that the source mentions and the knit has bound, so weft_put() is needed only for text a chunk prints with results = "asis", for a claim that travels with its value, and from a chunk that has no value of its own to show.

Usage

weft_put(...)

Arguments

...

Named values, or names of variables. An argument may be a call of claim().

Value

Inside a knit, NULL, invisibly. Outside one, the text of the block, of class weft_values, which prints as the text.

Details

Each argument publishes one name: weft_put(depth = mean(d$depth)), or weft_put(depth, n_sites) for variables of the same names. A name is ASCII letters, digits, _ and ., starting with a letter or _, at most 64 characters. An argument that is a call of claim() is captured: its checks are run and recorded with the value, nothing is stopped, and each check counts where the name is used.

A bool, a whole or decimal number, a string, a factor, a Date, an integer64 or an atomic vector of these (up to 10000 elements) is published with its kind. NA, NaN, Inf and NULL are published as missing. A value with units is refused, and any other object (a data frame, a list, a POSIXct, a function) is published as an error that is reported where the name is used.

In a knit with the hooks the block is written before the next block of prose, or at once in a chunk with results = "asis". Outside a knit nothing is stored: the text of the block is returned.

See also

weft_values_write()

Examples

depth <- c(1.5, 2.5, 6)
weft_put(depth_mean = mean(depth), n = length(depth))
#> ````{.weft-values}
#> {"weft":1,"lang":"r","run":null,"at":1794613173,"values":{"depth_mean":{"t":"float","v":"3.3333333333333335"},"n":{"t":"int","v":"3"}}}
#> ````
weft_put(depth_mean = claim(mean(depth), . > 1, . < 10))
#> ````{.weft-values}
#> {"weft":1,"lang":"r","run":null,"at":1794613173,"values":{"depth_mean":{"t":"float","v":"3.3333333333333335","checks":[{"text":". > 1","ok":true,"level":"fail","why":null},{"text":". < 10","ok":true,"level":"fail","why":null}]}}}
#> ````
